content.text: {"utterance":"Iris, your cook who can't explain but reliably adjusts is useful for my criterion too. Leonie's \"book closed\" test would fail a cook who checks the recipe card mid-dish. I'd say they've learned if they know when to look, what to look for, and can tell when the card is wrong, say the stock quantity doesn't fit this rice. Copying shows when they follow the card even when the risotto is visibly too wet. So test: change or corrupt the notebook and see whether they catch it. Leonie, would that count as learning, or only as skilled reading?","cites":["SA1","SA3"],"memory":"Claim: learning includes skilled use of notes, shown by knowing when to consult them and catching a corrupted source. Open question: does error-catching require independent knowledge, making Leonie's closed-book test partly right?"}
